bullets.title: MU: Blowout Q3 results, 16 SCAs signed, supply tight through 2027+
bullets.body: Micron delivered a massive beat on F3Q and raised Q4 guidance well above elevated expectations, briefly overtaking META and TSLA in market cap. Management signed 16 strategic customer agreements with take-or-pay volume commitments and pricing floors above prior peak gross margins; supply-demand imbalance expected to persist for years given CapEx of $40B+ in FY27 (Idaho 1, Tongluo online 2H27). HBM currently a gross margin drag but pricing expected to improve; semis sector surged +3.6% on the day.

bullets.title: AAPL: -6% on MacBook/iPad price hikes; skipping M6 for AI-focused M7
bullets.body: Apple announced 15–25% price increases on MacBooks and iPads, citing memory input cost pressures from rapid data center expansion, while skipping the high-end M6 chip to jump directly to an AI-focused M7 lineup. AAPL was the worst performer in the Mag 7 on the day, falling ~6.1–6.2%; iPhone prices were not raised but the door was left open for further moves.

bullets.title: MSFT: Technical Score 0 at 6.5-year relative lows; downside risk to $250
bullets.body: 22V Research flags MSFT with its worst Technical Score (0 of 4): stock is below a deteriorating 200-day MA since February 2026, down 18% since early June, and sitting at 6.5-year relative lows vs. the S&P 500. Support at 350–355 is expected to break, opening a measured-move target of $250; daily, weekly, and monthly momentum all negative.

bullets.title: ON/SYNA: onsemi acquires Synaptics in $7B all-stock deal, ~12% pro forma ownership
bullets.body: onsemi agreed to acquire Synaptics at a fixed exchange ratio of 1.350 ON shares per SYNA share (~$125.62/share implied), valuing the deal at ~$7B enterprise value. The transaction was unanimously approved by both boards, is expected to be accretive to non-GAAP EPS within 18 months with $200M in annual synergies, and is slated to close mid-2027.

bullets.title: QCOM: $5B FY27 datacenter guidance mostly inorganic (Alphawave); $15B FY29 target faces skepticism
bullets.body: Post-management-meeting notes show QCOM's FY27 $5B datacenter guidance is predominantly custom silicon from two hyperscale customers plus Alphawave inorganic contribution; AI200 revenue begins 2H FY27 with modest contribution while AI250 with HBC is the more impactful product. The $15B FY29 target drew skepticism; FY27 handset revenue expected to decline $5–6B y/y from memory challenges and iPhone revenue loss. Morgan Stanley upgraded QCOM to equal-weight from underweight with updated FY29 targets.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Sky unit nearing ~$2.2B acquisition of ITV Media & Entertainment business
bullets.body: Comcast's Sky unit is nearing an agreement to acquire ITV's Media & Entertainment business for approximately $2.2B, aimed at strengthening its UK streaming position. No additional financial details were disclosed in the digest.

bullets.title: CMCSA/CHTR: Broadband survey — cable subscriber attrition to continue; 2027 consensus looks unrealistic
bullets.body: KeyBanc's 2Q26 broadband survey finds Starlink is ~30% more expensive and ~30% slower than fiber/cable/FWA alternatives and represents only ~2% of the US market with no subscriber growth inflection. Cable satisfaction worsened vs. the prior survey (Comcast/Charter at 57% net satisfaction vs. fiber 69%/FWA 64%), and fiber/FWA represent a 50–60% penetration threat; 2027 net-add consensus for cable appears unrealistic.

bullets.title: OKLO: Guggenheim initiates Neutral; capital intensity and long FCF runway cited
bullets.body: Guggenheim initiated OKLO at Neutral, viewing the company as an early-stage IPP scaling from 75 MW at Q4 '27 to 1.1 GW by '32 with positive EBITDA not projected until 2030. Guggenheim's concern centers on the capital-intensive business model taking longer to generate free cash flow; the stock fell 5.6% on the day.

bullets.title: ACN: UBS maintains Buy at $275 PT; 8.5x 2Y fwd P/E near 20-year low, $10B cyber buildout
bullets.body: UBS hosted an expert call with a former Accenture executive and reiterates Buy with a $275 PT (16x 2028E EPS), noting ACN's 2Y forward P/E at 8.5x is the lowest in 20+ years. The firm is building a $10B cybersecurity business via ~$4.1B in M&A (Dragos, runZero, NetRise) and announced a $2B buyback boost to $7.5B total (~10% of market cap); AI transformation is seen accelerating faster than mobile/cloud cycles.

bullets.title: IOT (Samsara): KeyBanc reiterates Overweight; Tracking Label expands TAM, emerging products at 20% NNACV
bullets.body: KeyBanc reiterates Overweight on Samsara after its Beyond conference and investor day. The new Bluetooth Tracking Label ($15 list, consumption model) opens a non-fleet TAM including customers like Nvidia and Nike; emerging products now represent 20% of NNACV for three consecutive quarters with a medium-term target of 30%+. Current emerging products ARR is $150M, with Waste and Ground Intelligence having seven-figure deals in pipeline.

bullets.title: FIG: Wolfe reiterates Peer Perform post-Config 2026; fair value $15-$25
bullets.body: Wolfe Research maintained Peer Perform on Figma after Config 2026, flagging gross margin compression (down 11pp Y/Y to 82%) and that FY26 operating income was raised less than half the revenue beat. Config 2026 introduces Code Layers, Figma Motion, and agentic tools but Make drew mixed reviews and is not yet production-grade; weekly AI usage is still a minority of seats. Wolfe's fair value range is $15–$25 (4x–7x CY27E Sales), with the stock at 5x CY27 EV/Sales.

bullets.title: MRVL, SNOW, CCL: Hedgeye flags as top-30 longs on signal-strength model
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Risk Range™ fractal math model identifies MRVL, SNOW, and CCL among its highest-conviction long holdings ranked by time held, with positive signals across both TRADE (≤3 weeks) and TREND (3+ months) durations.

bullets.title: CZR: Louisiana May GGR +24% y/y, far ahead of JPM's +3% forecast
bullets.body: Caesars Louisiana properties delivered GGR of $55.3M in May, up 22.8% y/y, with Harrah's New Orleans +29.1% and Horseshoe Bossier City +39.2%; 2Q26 YTD tracking +24% y/y vs. JPM's +3% forecast. PENN Louisiana was flat at -1.8% y/y overall, with L'Auberge Baton Rouge down 16.5% offsetting L'Auberge du Lac +9.2%.

bullets.title: NVDA/Mag 7: Four names down double-digits YTD; Maleficent 7 index showing broad technical deterioration
bullets.body: 22V Research notes the Mag 7 index is beneath a cresting 40-week MA with negative momentum divergence; four of seven names are down double-digits YTD 2026. META and MSFT carry Technical Scores of 0, TSLA scores 1; the group is acting as a source of funds for the cyclical/breadth rotation.

bullets.title: INTC: Goldman Sachs initiates at Neutral
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs initiated coverage of Intel at Neutral, per the Technology Post-Market sector summary. No price target or detailed thesis was included in the digest items.

bullets.title: DELL: Downgraded to Hold from Buy at GF Securities
bullets.body: GF Securities downgraded Dell to Hold from Buy, as noted in the Technology Post-Market sector summary. DELL was among the notable hardware decliners on the day alongside AAPL, as input cost pressures weighed on PC-related names.

bullets.title: HPE: Goldman Sachs non-deal roadshow scheduled for July 9 in New York
bullets.body: HP Inc (HPE) is scheduled for a Goldman Sachs-hosted non-deal roadshow on July 9 in New York. Meeting request deadline was June 25.

bullets.title: MSFT: Xbox console prices raised globally for the third time, effective August 1
bullets.body: Microsoft is raising Xbox Series console prices worldwide for the third time, starting August 1, citing ongoing input cost pressures consistent with the broader memory crunch narrative.
